question: How often should I descale my espresso machine?
ground_truth: Every three months with normal use and medium-hardness water.

question: I have hard water and pull several shots a day. How often do I need to descale?
ground_truth: Every four to six weeks.

question: Why does descaling matter at all?
ground_truth: Minerals in the water leave limescale in the boiler and pipes, which reduces heating efficiency, weakens steam pressure and can eventually damage the machine. Regular descaling keeps the machine running well and protects the warranty.

question: Can I just use vinegar to descale the Brewline?
ground_truth: No. Never use vinegar, which leaves a lingering taste. Use Northwind food-safe descaling solution or another citric-acid-based descaler made for espresso machines.

question: What descaler is safe for the machine?
ground_truth: Northwind food-safe descaling solution, or another citric-acid-based descaler made for espresso machines.

question: What happens if I use a harsh chemical descaler?
ground_truth: Harsh chemical descalers can corrode internal parts and void the warranty, and damage from third-party harsh descaling chemicals is not covered.

question: Walk me through the descaling procedure.
ground_truth: Empty the water tank and mix one part descaling solution with the amount of water listed on the bottle, then pour it into the tank. Run one third of the tank through the group head, one third through the steam wand, let the machine sit for 15 minutes, then run the rest through both outlets.

question: What do I do right after a descaling cycle?
ground_truth: Remove and rinse the tank thoroughly, refill it with fresh water, and run two full tanks of clean water through the group head and steam wand before making coffee again.

question: How does the machine decide when to show a descaling reminder?
ground_truth: It bases the reminder on the water hardness setting you entered during setup.

question: What cleaning should I do after each coffee session?
ground_truth: Wipe the steam wand and purge it, and knock out the used puck.

question: What is the weekly cleaning routine?
ground_truth: Once a week, backflush the machine with plain water using the blind basket, and soak the portafilter and baskets in warm water with a little group head cleaner to remove coffee oils.

question: Will skipping descaling affect my warranty?
ground_truth: Yes. Damage from limescale buildup caused by skipped descaling is not covered by the warranty, and regular descaling protects it.

question: What comes in the box with the Brewline?
ground_truth: The machine, a portafilter with one single and one double basket, a 58mm tamper, a cleaning brush and a water hardness test strip.

question: Can I fill the tank with distilled water?
ground_truth: No. The machine needs some minerals to measure the water level correctly, so use fresh, cold water filled to the MAX line.

question: How long does the machine take to come up to temperature?
ground_truth: About 45 seconds, which is when the temperature light stops blinking.

question: Is there anything I should do before pulling my first shot?
ground_truth: Run a full tank of water through the group head and steam wand to prime and rinse the internal lines.

question: How many grams of coffee go in the double basket?
ground_truth: About 18 grams, distributed evenly and tamped level with firm pressure.

question: How long should a good double shot take to pour?
ground_truth: 25 to 30 seconds.

question: Where is the power switch on the machine?
ground_truth: On the right side of the machine.

question: How do I set the water hardness level?
ground_truth: Dip the included test strip in your water for one second, compare it to the chart in the manual, and set the water hardness level in the machine menu so it can remind you to descale at the right interval.

question: What temperature should steamed milk reach?
ground_truth: About 140 to 150 degrees Fahrenheit, which is when the pitcher becomes too hot to hold comfortably.

question: How do I steam milk with the wand?
ground_truth: Purge the wand for one second to clear condensation, submerge the tip just below the surface of cold milk, position the pitcher so the milk spins in a whirlpool, steam to about 140 to 150 degrees Fahrenheit, then wipe the wand immediately.

question: Is there anything to remove from the machine before first use?
ground_truth: Yes, remove all protective film and packaging before first use.

question: How do I fill the water tank the first time?
ground_truth: Lift the lid at the back of the machine, remove the tank, rinse it, fill it with fresh cold water up to the MAX line, and seat it firmly so the valve engages.

question: My machine will not turn on at all.
ground_truth: Confirm the power cable is fully seated in both the machine and the outlet and try a different outlet. Check the fuse in the plug where applicable. If there are still no lights, the thermal cutout may have tripped, so let the machine cool for 30 minutes and try again.

question: My shots pour really fast and taste weak.
ground_truth: That usually means the grind is too coarse or the dose too low. Grind finer, increase the dose slightly, tamp level with firm consistent pressure, and aim for a double shot that pours in 25 to 30 seconds.

question: Barely any coffee is coming out of the group head.
ground_truth: The grind is likely too fine or the basket overfilled, choking the machine. Grind coarser and reduce the dose. If it continues with fresh grounds, the shower screen may be clogged and need cleaning or a backflush.

question: The pump is loud but almost no water comes through.
ground_truth: The machine may be airlocked. Run water through the steam wand with the tank full to reprime the pump, and check that the tank valve is seated and the tank is not empty.

question: The steam wand hardly produces any steam.
ground_truth: Weak steam is usually a blocked steam tip: turn off and cool the machine, then clear each hole in the tip with the pin on the cleaning tool. A machine that has not been descaled in a long time can also lose steam power to limescale.

question: The temperature light keeps blinking and will not settle.
ground_truth: A continuously blinking temperature light after several minutes indicates a sensor fault. Turn the machine off and on once, and if it still blinks contact support with your order number, as the machine may need a warranty repair.

question: A different outlet did not revive my dead machine. What else can I try?
ground_truth: Check the fuse in the plug where applicable, then let the machine cool for 30 minutes in case the thermal cutout has tripped.

question: Should I grind finer or coarser when the machine chokes?
ground_truth: Coarser. A choking machine usually means the grind is too fine or the basket is overfilled, so grind coarser and reduce the dose.

question: Can a dirty shower screen slow my shots down?
ground_truth: Yes. If slow flow continues with fresh grounds, the shower screen may be clogged and need cleaning or a backflush.

question: How do I reprime the pump?
ground_truth: Run water through the steam wand with the water tank full.

question: Does tamping matter if my shot tastes weak?
ground_truth: Yes. Along with grinding finer and increasing the dose, make sure you are tamping level and with firm, consistent pressure.
